item.title: 11 years on, Pacific Meteorological leaders revisit Nuku’alofa declaration

item.content:encoded:
THE Pacific Meteorological Council (PMC) is meeting today in Tonga to revisit commitments first made more than a decade ago.

The meeting comes 11 years after Pacific ministers adopted the first Nuku’alofa Declaration in 2015, following efforts to bring meteorological directors and political leaders together to address challenges facing national meteorological services, making this years meeting especially important.

SPREP Director Climate Science and Information Salesa Nihmei said the PMC grew out of years of discussions among Pacific meteorological directors and ministers that had produced limited progress.

“Meteorological directors and ministers were meeting since 1993 and well into the 2000s,” Nihmei said.

“They would sit down and discuss their issues. And it went on like this for years until eventually some members became frustrated because nothing was moving.”

That frustration led to the establishment of the Pacific Meteorological Council in 2011.

Mr Nihmei said the council was created to provide a platform where Pacific meteorological services could collectively identify their priorities while also bringing development partners and technical institutions into the discussion.

“When we started the Council in 2011, from 54, and we’ve slowly grown in numbers and in 2023 we recorded over 240 people.”

The council’s role has also included making its activities more visible to potential donors and partners, with the aim of ensuring that organisations involved in development and technical support understand the challenges facing Pacific meteorological services.

The push to engage political leaders became more prominent from 2013, when meteorological directors sought greater understanding of the sector within governments.

Mr Nihmei said meteorological services are often housed within large government ministries whose primary responsibilities lie elsewhere, such as transport and infrastructure.

In response, ministers were brought together in 2015, resulting in the first Nuku’alofa Declaration.

Mr Nihmei said today’s meeting therefore represents more than another regional gathering: it provides an opportunity to return to commitments made 11 years ago and assess what has happened since.

item.title: Simla protest organisers work to finalise approvals

item.content:encoded:
ORGANISERS opposing the rezoning of Lot 32, Covuli Street,Simla,Lautoka are making steady progress toward a public demonstration while advancing multi-track legal steps to halt commercial development in the residential zone.Following the August 17 notice approving Amendment No. 177 to the City of Lautoka Town Planning Scheme, community leaders have shifted into active preparation to contest the transition.

Lautoka Residents and Ratepayers Association President Narayan Reddy confirmed that administrative steps for the upcoming march are nearly complete.“We will be, we have to get all the letters from the roads and all those authorities first, get their approval. And before the end of the month, we will be having the march,” he said. “The paperwork is ready, it’s just I have to lodge the paperwork application.”

Key milestones have already been reached as organizers coordinate municipal permits and build neighborhood consensus for the upcoming event. “The whole of Simla is supporting this. Nobody wants that project to be held in Simla. “It will be similar to what happened with the TNG protest.”Parallel progress is also unfolding on the legal front, despite dialogue with municipal officials remaining stalled.

“No word yet from council, they’re just blaming the town and country planning.”Formal complaints have already reached iFICAC , with further judicial measures prepared to ensure the community’s position is heard.

item.content:encoded:
Former Post Fiji chief executive officer Dr Anirudha Bansod’s appeal against conviction will be recalled on September 22 to reconfirm his position on appeal.

In 2024, Dr Bansod was sentenced to 18 months’ imprisonment after he was convicted of providing false confidentiality and conflict of interest declarations regarding the tender for the design, development, and implementation of the Post Fiji mobile application in 2022.

Dr Bansod has since served his sentence and returned to India.

Lawyer Jagath Karunaratne is representing Dr Bansod.

item.title: Mohammed Saneem’s Multi-Million-Dollar Lawsuit Set for First Court Appearance
item.description: Former Supervisor of Elections Mohammed Saneem’s multi-million-dollar civil action against several current and former State officials following his acquittal in a high-profile criminal case has been listed for its first call on September 16. A Writ of Summons and Statement of Claim filed in the High Court in Suva on June 29 under Civil Action No. 193 of 2026 states that Mr Saneem is seeking $5 mil
item.content:encoded:
Former Supervisor of Elections Mohammed Saneem’s multi-million-dollar civil action against several current and former State officials following his acquittal in a high-profile criminal case has been listed for its first call on September 16.

A Writ of Summons and Statement of Claim filed in the High Court in Suva on June 29 under Civil Action No. 193 of 2026 states that Mr Saneem is seeking $5 million in general damages, in addition to aggravated and exemplary damages.

Mr Saneem has named six defendants in the proceedings, including former acting Director of Public Prosecutions John Rabuku, whom he claims unlawfully sanctioned and authorised the charge against him. Mr Saneem claims Mr Rabuku’s appointment as acting DPP was itself unlawful, citing a Supreme Court ruling concerning eligibility requirements for the ODPP.

Current acting DPP Nancy Tikoisuva is also named as a defendant in her capacity as the prosecutor who conducted the proceedings against him in both the Magistrate’s Court and the High Court.

Former acting Police Commissioner Juki Fong Chew is accused of authorising and directing the investigation, arresting, and charging Mr Saneem without a reasonable basis. The writ also accuses Mr Juki Fong of failing to adequately supervise Criminal Investigation Department Officers Detective Sergeant Suliasi Dulaki and Detective Constable Tomasi Lagikula, who are also named as defendants for their roles in arresting, charging, and detaining him.

The Attorney-General is named as the sixth defendant as the nominal representative of the State, based on vicarious liability.

Mr Saneem and former attorney-general Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum were acquitted of all criminal charges relating to a variation agreement concerning Mr Saneem’s remuneration in June. The State has appealed the High Court’s decision to the Court of Appeal.

The lawsuit advances four causes of action, including false imprisonment. Mr Saneem alleges there was no reasonable or probable cause for his arrest because the criminal charge was based on an erroneous interpretation of the contract. He further claims detectives maliciously engineered a weekend detention by arresting him at 3 pm on a Friday, deliberately overlapping with his daughter’s birthday despite his good-faith offer to surrender on Monday morning.

He claims the defendants’ actions caused him significant mental distress, reputational damage, loss of professional income and substantial legal costs over a period exceeding two years.

Among the relief sought, Mr Saneem is seeking declarations that his constitutional rights were breached, and that the prosecution against him was instituted and continued maliciously and without reasonable and probable cause.

item.title: Goundar Shipping’s new fast ferry MV Captain Inoke
item.description: The High Court in Suva has granted Goundar Fast Ferries Pte Limited (GFF) leave to issue judicial review proceedings against state authorities regarding the delayed registration of its vessel, MV Captain Inoke. Justice Anjala Wati delivered the ruling today granting GFF leave to file judicial review proceedings within 28 days. The court also awarded GFF costs of $3500, payable by the respondents w
item.content:encoded:
The High Court in Suva has granted Goundar Fast Ferries Pte Limited (GFF) leave to issue judicial review proceedings against state authorities regarding the delayed registration of its vessel, MV Captain Inoke. Justice Anjala Wati delivered the ruling today granting GFF leave to file judicial review proceedings within 28 days. The court also awarded GFF costs of $3500, payable by the respondents within 14 days.

The respondents in the case include the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF), the Minister of Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport, the Prime Minister, and the Attorney-General. GFF applied for leave to challenge the continuous delay by the Minister in acting upon the recommendation of the MSAF Chief Executive Officer to approve the registration of the second-hand vessel. The vessel, purchased from the Republic of Korea, arrived in Suva in January 2025. Although MSAF initially refused the vessel’s registration on June 4, 2025, citing missing dry dock and survey reports, subsequent court documents revealed a significant shift in position.

Justice Wati noted that on September 1, 2025, the MSAF CEO had recommended that the Minister endorse and approve the vessel’s registration. However, the court found that the Minister failed to act on the CEO’s recommendation, causing an unreasonable delay of over six months without justification. The CEO’s assessment noted that the ship had undergone thorough safety and technical surveys culminating in a four-hour sea trial—and that 38 out of 39 identified defects were successfully resolved.

The senior surveyors concluded that the vessel was seaworthy and fit for carrying passengers and cargo on routes such as Natovi to Savusavu. Justice Wati ruled that the applicant presented an arguable case regarding the Minister’s delay, which potentially violated constitutional guarantees to prompt administrative action. Lawyer Siddharth Nandan (Nandan & Associates) represented GFF. The matter has been adjourned to November 3 for a mention.

item.content:encoded:
SELF-EMPLOYED businessman Imran Khan’s appeal against his conviction and sentence for possession of methamphetamine was called for the first time before the High Court in Suva this afternoon. The matter came before Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu this afternoon with the parties awaiting the court records to be furnished before the appeal proceeds. Khan, represented by lawyer Shayal Kant of Crown Law, filed Criminal Appeal No. 54 of 2026 on July 6, seeking an order setting aside his conviction and sentence or, alternatively, substituting the custodial sentence with a non-custodial penalty.

Khan was sentenced on June 30 by Magistrate Yogesh Prasad to four years and three months’ imprisonment, with a non-parole period of three years, after he was convicted of possessing 4.1364 grams of methamphetamine. The drugs were allegedly concealed in a modified water bottle inside his vehicle in 2023.

The appeal contains 30 grounds challenging the fairness of the trial process, the handling of evidence and the severity of the sentence imposed. One of the key issues raised by the defence concerns motor vehicle registration IV 991. The defence argues that the prosecution failed to produce critical documentary evidence, including Land Transport Authority records, to establish Khan’s ownership or exclusive control of the vehicle.

The defence has also challenged the Magistrate’s refusal to reopen the case after judgment was delivered, following an application based on what it described as new and material evidence. It argues that the refusal resulted in procedural unfairness and a miscarriage of justice.

The appeal further contends that the sentence imposed was manifestly excessive in the circumstances of the case. Khan will also file, through Kant, an application for bail pending the determination of his appeal. The matter has been adjourned to September 28.

item.content:encoded:
SUVA’S St Joseph’s Secondary School is proudly celebrating 70 years of education, faith, service and achievement this month.

The milestone marks seven decades of shaping young women and preparing them to contribute positively to their families, communities and Fiji.

Founded through the dedication of the Sisters of St Joseph of Cluny, the school has built a strong tradition of academic excellence, discipline and compassion.

The celebration has brought together past and present students, teachers, parents and supporters to honour its rich history.

item.title: Teachers likely paid
item.description: THE Fijian Teachers Association is assuming teachers at the center of unpaid salary reports have now been paid, despite receiving no confirmation from those affected. FTA’s general secretary Paula Manumanunitoga said the association had received no official complaint from teachers still waiting for their salaries.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fijian Teachers Association is assuming teachers at the center of unpaid salary reports have now been paid, despite receiving no confirmation from those affected.

FTA’s general secretary Paula Manumanunitoga said the association had received no official complaint from teachers still waiting for their salaries.

“I have not gotten any confirmation from any of those affected. But they are quiet. I believe they have received their pay,” he said.

Mr Manumanunitoga said no teacher had returned to the association to report that they remained unpaid.

“No official complaints have been filed yet about the unpaid salaries.”

As of Monday, 118 of the 134 affected teachers had been confirmed to have received their pay.
